title: Banana oat pancakes with smashed blueberries
summary: Three-ingredient pancakes sweetened only with banana: a breakfast the whole family can share.
texture: Soft, fluffy small pancakes, cut into strips or small pieces. Blueberries are smashed flat so there are no whole round berries.
ingredients: 1/2 cup quick oats, blended until fine
2 to 3 tbsp whole milk, if the batter is too thick (optional)
1/4 cup blueberries, smashed with a fork
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl, then whisk in the egg.
Stir in the blended oats. Let the batter rest 5 minutes to thicken; add a splash of milk if it's too thick to pour.
Warm a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat. Spoon in small pancakes, about 2 tablespoons each.
Cook 2 minutes until bubbles form, flip, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until cooked through in the middle.
Cool slightly, cut into strips or small pieces, and top with the smashed blueberries.
choking: Whole blueberries are a round-food choking risk for young toddlers: smash or quarter them.
Cut pancakes into strips or small pieces and skip syrup, which makes pieces stick together.

allergens.name: Egg
allergens.note: Make sure egg has been introduced before serving this recipe.

allergens.name: Milk (if used)
allergens.note: Whole cow's milk is fine in food and as a drink from 12 months. Leave it out or use water if your child avoids dairy.

storage: Fridge up to 2 days, or freeze with parchment between pancakes up to 1 month. Reheat in a toaster or pan, then cool before serving.
tips: Oats are naturally gluten-free but are often processed alongside wheat. Choose certified gluten-free oats if your child needs to avoid gluten.
Honey is safe from 12 months, but these don't need it: ripe banana does the sweetening.

photo.alt: Small banana oat pancakes topped with smashed blueberries
